context: Two salarymen chat about their company's long-running employment policies
purpose: Teach: 中小/従業/掛け/ポスト/サラリーマン/適正/大半/にわたって

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: うちの会社って、戦後を通じて長年にわたってずっと終身雇用を守ってきた珍しい中小企業なんだよな。
lines.en: Our company is a rare mid-sized firm that has maintained lifetime employment for many years throughout the postwar period.
lines.style: Reflective male office worker tone, slightly nostalgic and matter-of-fact.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 確かに。従業員の大半が二十年以上勤めてるって、今どき信じられないですよね。
lines.en: True. Most of the employees have been here over twenty years — pretty unbelievable these days.
lines.style: Polite junior colleague tone, mildly impressed and conversational.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: そうそう。年功序列に掛けてきた経営方針が、結局今のご時世まで生き残ってるんだから不思議だよ。
lines.en: Exactly. It's strange that their bet on seniority-based management has survived into the present age.
lines.style: Casual senior salaryman musing, mixing admiration with slight skepticism.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: でも、適正な評価がされにくいって若手からは不満も出てますよ。
lines.en: But younger staff complain that fair evaluation is hard to come by under this system.
lines.style: Polite but candid junior tone, raising a concern diplomatically.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: わかるよ。俺らみたいな平均的なサラリーマンには安心だけど、優秀な奴ほど物足りないんだろうな。
lines.en: I get it. It's reassuring for average salarymen like us, but the talented ones surely want more.
lines.style: Self-deprecating older colleague tone, sympathetic and a bit resigned.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: ポスト争いもほとんどないですし、上がつかえてるから昇進も遅いんですよね。
lines.en: There's barely any competition for posts, and promotions are slow because senior positions are jammed.
lines.style: Polite junior voicing frustration in restrained workplace register.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: まあ、それも一種の安定の代償ってやつだな。明日も会議、頑張ろうや。
lines.en: Well, that's the price of stability, I suppose. Let's push through tomorrow's meeting too.
lines.style: Warm closing remark from senior, casual and encouraging.
